name: delay_calls_0ee8
comment: Writes the byte 0x64 to XDATA 0x0A56 as a loop counter, calls 0x0EE8 to load and start Timer 1, waits for its overflow, and calls 0x0EE8 again on the next pass. The counter is written once and read back per pass, so the wait is counted rather than fixed. 0x64 is the data value written, not an address.

name: mentions_absent_target
comment: Calls 0xBEEF, which is named here to pin that a comment naming an address the listings do not carry produces no citation: the tool must refuse the row rather than invent a callee for it.

name: chan_arm_1709
comment: One arm of a three-function family. On bit 1 of 0xE3 it loads DPTR with 0x0A56, calls 0x07D0 to read the byte the pointer selects, and then writes 0x0F, 0x60, 0x00, 0x00 and 0x00 to XDATA 0x0A56-0x0A5A before returning. The two addresses in the first two clauses are the same four-digit tokens the last clause names as bytes.

name: chan_arm_1708
comment: The other arm of the same family, reading 0x1708. On the same bit it calls 0x07D0, clears the direct byte 0xAA and sets bit 4 of 0x1106, which is the call 0x018C's arm also makes. The shared helper here is 0x5A43.

name: reset_entry
comment: The reset vector's target. Sets the stack pointer to 0xC0, writes 0x3F to XDATA 0x1001, then calls to 0x110A, 0x158E, 0x0F75, 0x1594 and 0x00CF before tail-jumping into the copy loops that follow.

name: keil_index_helper
comment: Multiplies A by B and adds the product to DPTR. The 0x07D0 sites reach it with B loaded from a record stride; that 0x07D0 is this image's own XDATA byte and not the common-area function at 0x07D0, which is a different program's address.

name: wait_then_jump_0d40
comment: Polls the status byte at XDATA 0x0724 and, whichever way that test falls, it ends in an sjmp to 0x0D40. The listing carries that sjmp at 0x0D27. `call_graph.py` scans the four absolute transfer forms and not this one, so 0x0D40 is a citation with no inbound edge and no row in the table, and the frame guard reads the verb and credits it anyway.
